newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane cascades further in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane cascades further in late trade.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices continued to cascade in late trade on Thursday, the second day of a free fall helped along by weak NYMEX futures, traders said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, spot propane fell a further one cent to between 47.25 cents and 47.50 cents a gallon, nearly 3.75 cents below early Wednesday levels.
Conway, Kansas, hub also shed another quarter cent to 47.50/48.25 cents, 1.75 cents since the opening Wednesday before the free fall began.
"It all began when some players thought they sensed a bearish sentiment in the market with these imports coming in and the market began to fall," said one Houston broker.
About seven cargoes are expected to arrive in the U.S. Gulf Coast begining later this month.
February Belvieu barrels traded Thursday for 43.50 cents, considered one of the lowest values in relation to crude, which ended down 81 cents at $24.26 a barrel.
"With our tight supplies and the way demand has been going, buying February is not a bad idea," said one Houston player.
Much of the market has been buying hand to mouth given lean inventories, the lowest since 1970.
Midwest traders said propane largely followed Belvieu south, but several end-users were also in the market selling barrels.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
